title: GitHub Octoverse 2026: AI Agents, Citizen Developers, and the New Security Reality
content_md: TL;DR Code is being written three times faster than anyone can review it : GitHub logged 34.3 billion commits this year, up from 12.9 billion, and more than 40% of pull requests now start with an AI agent, not a human. The newest developers are not developers : Citizen coders now ship apps wired to business systems with API keys they have never been taught to protect. Claude Code-assisted commits already leak secrets more often than human-made commits. A leaked key outlives your whole security program : 64% of credentials found valid were still valid more than four years later. See which controls actually keep pace with agents, automation, and everyone who can now ship code. Every year, we look forward to GitHub's State of the Octoverse report. It is one of the best leading indicators of where software development is heading, and what the rest of the technology industry can expect in the coming years. This year's report is especially exciting, and the numbers are staggering. Over the past year, developers generated 34.3 billion commits across GitHub, up from 12.9 billion the previous year. That is nearly three times the activity in just one year. Even more remarkable, over 40% of pull requests now start with an AI agent, up from just 17% six months earlier. GitHub Actions also executed more than 45 billion jobs, over three times the previous year's total. These numbers signal a fundamental change in who creates software and how quickly it gets built.
